# PancreaticMass Clinical Compass
## Pancreatic Mass Insurance Authorization Guide

[Button: Back to Assessment] (navigates to /pancreaticmass)

---

## Procedure Codes (CPT Codes)

### CPT 43242 — RVU 5.00
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy, flexible, transoral; with transendoscopic ultrasound-guided intramural or transmural fine needle aspiration/biopsy(s)
Device/Access: Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS) with FNA
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Endoscopic ultrasound examination
- Fine needle aspiration/biopsy of pancreatic mass
Note: Used for diagnostic sampling of pancreatic masses.

### CPT 43238 — RVU 4.50
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy, flexible, transoral; with transendoscopic ultrasound-guided intramural or transmural fine needle aspiration/biopsy(s), (includes endoscopic ultrasound examination limited to the esophagus, stomach or duodenum, and adjacent structures)
Device/Access: Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS) with FNA
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Endoscopic ultrasound examination of esophagus, stomach, duodenum
- Fine needle aspiration/biopsy of adjacent structures
Note: Similar to 43242, often used for lesions in specific areas.

### CPT 48150 — RVU 40.00
Pancreatectomy, proximal subtotal with total duodenectomy, partial gastrectomy, cholecystectomy, and jejunostomy; with pancreaticojejunostomy
Device/Access: Surgical Resection
Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):
- Removal of pancreatic head, duodenum, gallbladder, part of stomach
- Reconstruction of digestive tract
Note: Commonly known as the Whipple procedure, used for resectable pancreatic head tumors.

---

## ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes

- C25.0 (Primary) — Malignant neoplasm of head of pancreas — Primary malignant tumor located in the head of the pancreas.
- C25.1 (Primary) — Malignant neoplasm of body of pancreas — Primary malignant tumor located in the body of the pancreas.
- C25.2 (Primary) — Malignant neoplasm of tail of pancreas — Primary malignant tumor located in the tail of the pancreas.
- C25.9 — Malignant neoplasm of pancreas, unspecified — Primary malignant tumor of the pancreas where the specific location is not documented.
- D13.6 — Benign neoplasm of pancreas — Non-cancerous growth or tumor of the pancreas.
- K86.1 — Other chronic pancreatitis — Chronic inflammation of the pancreas, which can sometimes present as a mass.

(Codes marked "Primary" are required = true.)

---

## Payer-Specific Authorization Requirements

### Medicare
Status Badges: No Prior Auth (FFS); Covered with Medical Necessity
Prior Auth Note: Medicare generally covers medically necessary diagnostic and treatment services for pancreatic masses, including EUS-FNA and Whipple procedures, when criteria are met. Specific coverage may depend on National and Local Coverage Determinations (NCDs/LCDs).
Overview: Medicare Part B covers outpatient services, including physician services, and Part A covers inpatient hospital stays. Coverage for pancreatic mass evaluation and treatment is typically provided when deemed medically necessary by a physician and aligns with established guidelines.

Coverage Criteria:
- EUS-FNA:
  - Presence of a pancreatic mass or lesion identified by other imaging (e.g., CT, MRI).
  - Need for tissue diagnosis to determine malignancy or specific pathology.
- Whipple Procedure (48150):
  - Diagnosis of resectable pancreatic head adenocarcinoma or other suitable periampullary tumors.
  - Patient deemed surgically fit with no evidence of distant metastasis.

Required Documentation:
- General:
  - Detailed clinical history and physical examination notes.
  - Results of prior imaging studies (CT, MRI, ultrasound).
  - Pathology reports from any previous biopsies.
- For Surgery:
  - Surgical consultation notes outlining the plan and rationale.
  - Pre-operative assessments (cardiac, pulmonary, nutritional).

Submission Process:
1. Physician submits claims directly to Medicare.
2. Ensure all documentation supports medical necessity.

Common Denial Reasons:
- Lack of medical necessity documentation.
- Services considered experimental or investigational.
- Incorrect coding or billing.

Known Payer Policies:
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| CMS | Covered | NCDs and LCDs apply for specific diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. |

Reimbursement Note: Reimbursement rates are set by CMS and may vary based on geographic location and facility type.

Authorization Tips:
- Verify patient eligibility and benefits prior to services.
- Maintain thorough and accurate medical records.

### Medicaid
Status Badges: Prior Auth Required; Prior Authorization Required
Prior Auth Note: Medicaid coverage for pancreatic mass evaluation and treatment typically requires prior authorization. Policies vary significantly by state. It is crucial to check state-specific Medicaid guidelines.
Overview: Medicaid provides health coverage to low-income individuals and families. Coverage for pancreatic mass services is generally available if medically necessary, but strict adherence to state-specific prior authorization processes and medical necessity criteria is enforced.

Coverage Criteria:
- General:
  - Medical necessity established by a physician.
  - Adherence to state-specific clinical guidelines for diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.
- EUS-FNA:
  - Documentation of a suspicious pancreatic lesion.
  - Failure of less invasive diagnostic methods or their contraindication.
- Whipple Procedure (48150):
  - Confirmed diagnosis of resectable pancreatic cancer.
  - Comprehensive pre-operative evaluation demonstrating patient suitability and absence of metastatic disease.

Required Documentation:
- Prior Authorization:
  - Prior authorization request form.
  - Clinical notes, imaging reports, and pathology results supporting medical necessity.
  - Treatment plan.
- Claims Submission:
  - All documentation submitted for prior authorization.
  - Operative reports for surgical procedures.

Submission Process:
1. Submit prior authorization request to the state Medicaid agency.
2. Await approval before performing non-emergent procedures.
3. Submit claims with approved authorization number.

Common Denial Reasons:
- Lack of prior authorization.
- Incomplete or insufficient documentation of medical necessity.
- Services not covered under the specific state Medicaid plan.

Known Payer Policies:
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| State Medicaid (e.g., California Medi-Cal) | Varies by State | Specific policies for oncology and advanced diagnostic procedures must be consulted. |

Reimbursement Note: Reimbursement rates are typically lower than Medicare or private insurance and are determined by each state’s Medicaid program.

Authorization Tips:
- Always obtain prior authorization in advance.
- Be familiar with your state’s specific Medicaid policies for oncology.

### Private Insurance
Status Badges: Prior Auth Required; Prior Authorization Required
Prior Auth Note: Most private insurance plans require prior authorization for advanced diagnostic procedures like EUS-FNA and major surgeries such as the Whipple procedure. Coverage criteria vary widely by plan and insurer.
Overview: Private insurance plans offer diverse coverage for pancreatic mass evaluation and treatment. While most medically necessary services are covered, prior authorization is a standard requirement. Patients may have deductibles, co-pays, and co-insurance.

Coverage Criteria:
- General:
  - Evidence of a pancreatic mass requiring further investigation or treatment.
  - Clinical guidelines and evidence-based medicine supporting the chosen intervention.
- EUS-FNA:
  - Imaging findings (CT, MRI) suggestive of a pancreatic mass.
  - Need for histological diagnosis for treatment planning.
- Whipple Procedure (48150):
  - Resectable pancreatic or periampullary malignancy confirmed by biopsy.
  - Multi-disciplinary team evaluation confirming surgical candidacy.

Required Documentation:
- Prior Authorization:
  - Completed prior authorization form with CPT and ICD-10 codes.
  - Physician’s order and detailed clinical notes.
  - All relevant diagnostic reports (imaging, lab, pathology).
- Appeals:
  - Letter of medical necessity from treating physician.
  - Peer-reviewed literature supporting the treatment.

Submission Process:
1. Submit prior authorization request through the insurer’s portal or fax.
2. Follow up regularly on authorization status.
3. Submit claims after services are rendered, ensuring all codes match authorization.

Common Denial Reasons:
- Lack of prior authorization or expired authorization.
- Services deemed not medically necessary or experimental.
- Out-of-network provider or facility.
- Incomplete or conflicting documentation.

Known Payer Policies:
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| Aetna | Covered with Medical Necessity | EUS is covered for evaluating pancreatic abnormalities and staging tumors (CPB 0446). |
| Cigna | Covered with Medical Necessity | Whipple surgery for pancreatic cancer is covered when medically appropriate. |

Reimbursement Note: Reimbursement varies significantly by plan, network status, and negotiated rates. Patients are responsible for deductibles, co-insurance, and co-pays.

Authorization Tips:
- Always verify benefits and obtain prior authorization.
- Document all communication with the insurance company.
- Be prepared to appeal denials with strong clinical justification.
